analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md; no executable code, so no direct security regression is possible from this diff. The changes I examined, on head lines 619-625 and 869-905, describe out-of-order measurement handling and freshness anchoring in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate, plus three TTFT admission estimator corrections (per-step decode pricing, idle-rate bounds, a 30-minute evidence expiry) with the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback.

Relevant threat model areas are TB-002, TB-007 and T-010/T-029 for availability and admission, and T-041 for the prefix cache. The prefix-cache text in this file (TTL, SSD tier, cache scope) is unchanged or only context. Nothing here alters the T-041 posture, which covers the 30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags and coordinator-authored scope. Nothing here touches App Attest (TB-011), attestation (TB-009), the fan helper (TB-010) or key custody.

One point worth a later look: the documented estimator changes lower projected processing time, so first-content deadline admission becomes more permissive. That is a performance and availability trade-off, not a confidentiality or integrity issue. The docs state that actual deadline expiry and physical memory admission still apply, and a kill-switch env var exists. The estimator code itself (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, CBv2DecodeRateShape) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that it matches the docs; that is a coverage limit rather than a finding. The documented rate/EWMA inputs are provider-local numeric measurements, not consumer-controlled in a way that would let a consumer game them, but I did not verify this against code. No findings.
